title: A Data-Driven Closed-Loop Control Approach to Drive Neural State Transitions for Mechanistic Insight.
publication_status: Peer-reviewed journal article; Human Brain Mapping; 2026
domain: Neuroimaging; affective neuroscience; individualized fMRI dynamics and control
dataset_or_cohort: Reanalysis of Zamoscik et al. remitted major depressive disorder cohort from Heidelberg
sample_scale: 60 participants: 30 remitted MDD and 30 matched healthy controls; two 4.5-minute scans per person
split_strategy: Within each participant and condition, the first 120 time points trained the DSR model and the final 40 formed the test segment; five independently initialized models were fitted and the lowest-test-loss model was selected, so the test segment participated in model selection.
observation_process: 3 T Siemens fMRI; TR 1.5 seconds; rest and sad-mood induction; 11 bilateral ROIs reduced to 66 principal-component features
missingness: No explicit missing-data model was reported; preprocessing produced complete modeled segments after nuisance removal and band-pass filtering.
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: no clinical time-to-event outcome; each scan is a fixed-length sequence
state: Individual nonlinear latent neural state reconstructed by a shallow piecewise-linear recurrent neural network from 66 regional principal-component signals.
observation_decoder: A linear decoder maps latent state to 66-dimensional regional fMRI observations; affective target states are represented by Gaussian-mixture distributions.
action: Additive state-dependent latent control restricted globally or to selected regions
action_provenance: Simulated model control; not an administered physiological stimulation
transition_mechanism: Individual shallow piecewise-linear recurrent neural dynamics coupled to an optimized state-feedback controller toward a Gaussian-mixture target.
maximum_horizon: Main controlled trajectories run T=D+11 steps with D=10 (21 steps total, approximately 31.5 s at TR 1.5 s); D=5 is reported as a sensitivity analysis. The DSR train/test segments contain 120/40 observed points per condition.
rollout_regime: Free generative reconstruction and simulated closed-loop control from empirical initial states
capability_claim: Planning: optimize controls that move reconstructed brain dynamics between rest and sad-mood targets
baselines: Uncontrolled (zero-control) dynamics, rMDD-versus-healthy-control models, and 11 region-restricted control solutions; no separate action-agnostic learned predictive model.
state_fidelity_metrics: Held-out reconstruction, power-spectrum Hellinger distance, and empirical-versus-reconstructed functional-connectivity agreement.
transition_metrics: Target negative log likelihood over controlled trajectories, cumulative control energy, target convergence, and Lyapunov characterization of reconstructed dynamics.
rollout_stability: Target likelihood is traced over controlled trajectories and conclusions are stress-tested at D=5 versus D=10; no formal long-horizon drift, joint-state coherence, or physiological constraint-violation audit.
action_sensitivity: Zero-control comparison, control restricted to each of 11 bilateral regions, and control-horizon/regularization sensitivity; no empirical stimulation-response validation.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Variation across independently initialized models is examined, but no reliability, ECE, calibration slope, predictive interval, or interval-coverage calibration is reported.
external_validation: No external, temporal, or institutional validation; authors identify single-dataset generalizability as a limitation
decision_utility: Simulated target attainment and energy quantify control feasibility; no clinician or patient decision outcome
safety_evaluation: No clinical hazard, physiological constraint, failure-recovery, or override evaluation
statistical_analysis: Mann-Whitney U tests, Pearson correlations, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control, and IQR outlier handling
causal_language: Authors describe model-based causal intervention analyses and mechanistic insight, but interventions occur only in a learned latent model
estimand: Model-specific individual controlled trajectory and target proximity; no identified real-world treatment-effect estimand
confounding_strategy: NA: the study does not estimate a real stimulation treatment effect; simulated latent controls have no design-based confounding adjustment.
positivity_and_overlap: NI: overlap/support for latent controls was not evaluated
counterfactual_validation: Only internal model interventions and regional perturbations; no randomized or empirical counterfactual validation
code_access: Public code and analysis repository: https://github.com/humml-lab/fmri-control; MIT license
weights_access: Unclear: checkpoint-consuming scripts are present, but study-specific trained weights were not clearly released
data_access: Paper reports fully preprocessed data with the code; raw participant data access is governed by the original study
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed ROI, PCA, filtering, model-training, and control procedures plus public analysis code/preprocessed arrays; reconstruction from raw scanner data is only partial.
randomness: Five Xavier-initialized models per participant; best test loss selected; fixed random seeds not reported
evidence_anchors: Human Brain Mapping PMCID PMC13370802: Methods 5.2-5.3 (DSR and control), Results Figs. 2-6, Supplementary Figs. S4 and S12, Limitations, and Data Availability; official humml-lab/fmri-control repository.
appraisal_strengths: Individual models, held-out sequence reconstruction, free controlled trajectories, explicit zero-control/region perturbations, horizon sensitivity, and public code/preprocessed data.
appraisal_limitations: Small single-site cohort; the final test segment participates in model selection; abstract latent controls lack a physiological dose mapping, empirical intervention validation, formal calibration, external validation, and hazard testing.
source_status: Primary peer-reviewed full text and supplementary captions inspected; official code/data repository checked.

title: A digital twin for hospital antimicrobial resistance forecasting and constrained intervention optimisation
domain: Hospital epidemiology; antimicrobial resistance; synthetic contact-network digital twin
dataset_or_cohort: Author-developed synthetic hospital simulator under canonical, partial-observation, shock, superspreader, surveillance, and distribution-shift regimes
sample_scale: 10 wards, 200 patients, 300 staff; 60-day canonical and 360-day shifted trajectories; 12 independent replicates per family
institution_count: NA: fully synthetic hospital rather than an observed institutional cohort
split_strategy: Trajectory-level train/validation/test partitions with disjoint simulator seed ranges; matched counterfactual branches share initial state and exogenous random stream
observation_process: Daily directed weighted patient-staff contact graphs; patient/staff attributes, admissions, antibiotic exposure, infection/resistance, isolation, screening and surveillance
missingness: Partial-observation experiments explicitly delay, reduce, or compress surveillance; no real-world missing-data mechanism
censoring_or_competing_events: Admissions, discharges and importation are generated by the simulator; no observational censoring problem
state: Daily hospital graph with node features, ward/contact structure, colonization/infection/resistance status, antibiotic exposure and containment state
observation_decoder: Forecast of endogenous spread versus importation and intervention-conditioned future resistant burden/action ranking
action: Library of hospital-wide screening and isolation policies subject to budgets, maximum-use and cooldown constraints
action_provenance: Explicit simulated screening/isolation policies applied to cloned hospital states
transition_mechanism: Mechanistic agent/contact simulator plus GraphSAGE and temporal transformer forecasting; MILP selects a constrained policy
maximum_horizon: 7 observed days to forecast or branch 7 future days
rollout_regime: Learned fixed-H=7 forecasts from branched simulator states; matched policy evaluation uses a common past and common exogenous random stream, while the mechanistic hospital simulator—not the learned forecaster—runs freely.
capability_claim: Planning: forecast action-conditioned outcomes and optimize constrained screening/isolation policy
baselines: Predictive baselines and feature/contact ablations; baseline containment protocol serves as no-change comparator
state_fidelity_metrics: AUROC, accuracy, F1, sensitivity and specificity for spread-source classification
transition_metrics: Within-state action-ranking accuracy, top-2 accuracy, strict improvement, non-worsening rate, regret and AUROC
rollout_stability: Distribution-shift and surveillance stress tests; non-worsening and regret reported; no formal long-horizon learned-model drift curve
action_sensitivity: Ground-truth versus partial observation, contact-weight and node-feature ablations, delayed/frequent surveillance changes, and multiple policy actions
calibration_and_uncertainty: Threshold fragility under shift is discussed; no reliability diagram, ECE, slope/intercept, or interval-coverage calibration
external_validation: Only synthetic regime shifts and retraining/zero-shot transfer; no external hospital or simulated-to-real validation
decision_utility: Seventy held-out states support action ranking; MILP demonstrates constrained policy selection in simulation
safety_evaluation: Containment burden and non-worsening are measured; budget/max-use/cooldown constraints and stress regimes are tested; no clinical deployment safety
statistical_analysis: Independent replicates, held-out seed ranges and reported performance distributions; exact inferential test details are limited
causal_language: The paper labels a causal/intervention branch and generates matched counterfactual futures from identical states
estimand: Baseline-relative 7-day resistant-infection burden and policy value within the specified simulator
confounding_strategy: Simulator structure and matched exogenous random streams remove simulated confounding; no real-world confounding analysis
positivity_and_overlap: Within-simulator actions are available by construction; real-hospital positivity/overlap is NA
counterfactual_validation: Matched simulator branches provide synthetic counterfactual ground truth only
weights_access: Unclear: pretrained learned-model weights were not stated as released
data_access: Publicly regenerable synthetic trajectories and driver scripts; no real patient data
preprocessing_reproducibility: Simulator, feature construction, seed partitions and model/optimization workflow are described and coded
randomness: Disjoint seed ranges and 12 independent replicates are reported
evidence_anchors: medRxiv version 1 full text: Methods on the synthetic hospital, T=7/H=7 temporal graph task, partial observation, common-state/common-noise intervention branching, and constrained MILP; Results on surveillance and distribution shifts and within-state policy ranking; Code Availability links the predictive and causal repositories.
appraisal_strengths: Matched branches, explicit action library, action baselines, stress tests and constrained optimization
appraisal_limitations: Preprint-only and entirely synthetic evidence; the learned forecaster is fixed-horizon rather than recursively free-running; no real-hospital validation, formal calibration, or clinical deployment hazard evaluation.

title: CardamomOT: a mechanistic optimal transport-based framework for gene regulatory network inference, trajectory reconstruction and generative modeling

dataset_or_cohort: Accessible abstract plus official repository experimental datasets: Schiebinger mouse reprogramming, Semrau mouse embryonic stem cells, Kameneva human sympathoadrenal development, and in-silico network benchmarks
sample_scale: Official repository materials document synthetic FN4/FN8/CN5/BN8 systems and experimental series spanning 5 days, 4 stages/97 genes, and 18 time points/108 genes; exact cell counts and complete paper-level totals are NI because the bioRxiv full text was inaccessible.
institution_count: NA: public experimental and simulated datasets rather than a clinical institutional cohort
split_strategy: NI: full paper split protocol unavailable; official repository contains Schiebinger data_train.h5ad and data_test.h5ad, full datasets for other examples, and repeated benchmark result files
observation_process: Time-labeled scRNA-seq snapshots with gene counts; exact labels and literature RNA/protein kinetic-rate priors
missingness: NI: manuscript treatment of missing genes/cells/dropout could not be inspected; repository documents required AnnData inputs and zero-inflated/negative-binomial mixture components
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: no clinical censoring or competing-event outcome
state: Observed RNA counts plus latent proteins, kinetic parameters, cell-time distributions and inferred GRN state
observation_decoder: Reconstructed RNA/protein trajectories, GRN edges/velocity fields, and generated single-cell datasets under wild type or perturbation
action: Exogenous stimulus schedules and virtual gene knockout, partial knockout and overexpression
action_provenance: Simulated modifications of calibrated regulatory interactions; not administered interventions in a prospective experiment
transition_mechanism: Mechanistic transcriptional-bursting and translation/degradation model calibrated by optimal transport across time snapshots
maximum_horizon: Up to day 18 in the Schiebinger real-data example; NI: manuscript-wide maximum horizon could not be verified
rollout_regime: Free-running mechanistic simulation from a calibrated GRN; official artifacts compare simulated and observed temporal distributions
capability_claim: Action-conditioned simulation: predict cellular trajectories under unseen regulatory perturbations
baselines: Official result scripts compare CardamomOT with CARDAMOM1, GENIE3, Pearson, PIDC, SINCERITIES and reference-fitting variants
state_fidelity_metrics: Abstract reports GRN and trajectory reconstruction; repository contains score arrays, marginal comparisons, UMAPs and simulated-versus-data checks
transition_metrics: Trajectory score/loss arrays and velocity/trajectory reconstruction artifacts; NI: exact metric definitions and numerical paper results were not verifiable from full text
rollout_stability: Generated temporal marginal and UMAP checks are available; NI: formal stability/constraint analysis in the paper could not be verified
action_sensitivity: Repository includes stimulus disabling/strength settings, KO, 50-percent KO and overexpression artifacts with wild-type simulations
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI: no formal calibration or interval-coverage result could be verified in accessible abstract or official artifacts
external_validation: Multiple published experimental datasets are demonstrated, but models are fitted per dataset; no frozen external cohort was verified
decision_utility: No clinical or operational decision-utility evaluation; biological hypothesis generation is proposed
safety_evaluation: NA: no clinical/physical deployment safety claim or hazard test
statistical_analysis: NI: exact statistical tests could not be inspected; official results include five- and ten-run benchmark artifacts
causal_language: The abstract claims prediction of responses to unseen perturbations by modifying inferred regulatory interactions; this is a model-based counterfactual claim, not an identified treatment effect.
estimand: No explicit population or individual causal estimand could be verified; outputs are simulated responses under specified GRN edits.
confounding_strategy: NI: manuscript assumptions for causal identification/confounding could not be inspected
positivity_and_overlap: NI: perturbation support/overlap discussion could not be inspected
counterfactual_validation: In-silico ground truth and generated KO/overexpression artifacts provide model-domain checks; experimental perturbation ground truth was not verified
code_access: Public official repository: https://github.com/eliasventre/CardamomOT; installation, pipeline, tests, and article-result scripts are inspectable, but no repository license metadata was detected.
weights_access: Public calibrated arrays and weights.npy files are included in official experimental and article-result directories
data_access: Public processed AnnData examples, train/test files, simulated benchmarks and result artifacts are included
preprocessing_reproducibility: Repository documents installation, full pipeline, kinetic-rate provenance, stimulus schedules and reproduction scripts; paper-only details remain NI
randomness: Repeated benchmark and five-run GRN artifacts are present; NI: fixed seed policy could not be verified
evidence_anchors: Accessible primary evidence: bioRxiv v2 abstract/version metadata for DOI 10.64898/2026.03.31.715390 and the official eliasventre/CardamomOT README, configs, dataset modules, tests, experimental_datasets, and article-result scripts. Direct v2 PDF/HTML requests returned HTTP 429 on 2026-09-12.
appraisal_strengths: Mechanistic executable model, multiple real and simulated datasets, public code/data/calibrated artifacts, and explicit perturbation files
appraisal_limitations: Full-text-only sample counts, metric definitions, statistical procedures, causal assumptions, and paper tables remain NI because bioRxiv returned HTTP 429; repository evidence was not used to invent those details.
source_status: Primary abstract/version metadata and official repository inspected; full primary text inaccessible from the lawful public endpoint (HTTP 429).

title: DITTO: A Visual Digital Twin for Interventions and Temporal Treatment Outcomes in Head and Neck Cancer.
publication_status: Peer-reviewed IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics article; author preprint arXiv:2407.13107 inspected
domain: Oncology; head-and-neck cancer; visual clinical decision support
dataset_or_cohort: MD Anderson retrospective squamous oropharyngeal cancer cohort, plus a symptom-model cohort
sample_scale: Main text reports 526 patients; appendix reports 536 with 389 development and 147 evaluation; separate symptom cohort n=937
split_strategy: Appendix A.2 reports 389 development and 147 evaluation patients (total 536), whereas the main text reports 526; the symptom model uses an 80/20 split. The internal total-count inconsistency is unresolved and preserved.
observation_process: Longitudinal baseline, tumor/nodal response, dose-limiting toxicity and treatment decisions; survival/recurrence/toxicity follow-up
missingness: Input dropout is used to tolerate missing features; missing symptom values are omitted from MSE; no full missingness mechanism
censoring_or_competing_events: Survival models use time-to-event and last follow-up; incomplete censoring treatment is acknowledged as a limitation
state: Patient features, disease/tumor state, response, toxicity and sequential treatment history
observation_decoder: Next-stage response/toxicity and long-term overall survival, locoregional control, distant metastasis, feeding-tube use and aspiration
action: Induction chemotherapy, concurrent chemotherapy and neck dissection across three sequential decisions
action_provenance: Observed clinician treatments in retrospective records; alternative treatment sequences simulated in the digital twin
transition_mechanism: Learned transition models, deep survival mixture models and DQN/transformer policy models
maximum_horizon: Three treatment decisions; toxicity at 6 months and disease outcomes to 5 years; survival metrics at 12, 24, 36 and 48 months
rollout_regime: Offline sequential patient simulation and policy/counterfactual visualization
capability_claim: Planning: compare and select sequential treatment plans using learned digital-twin outcomes
baselines: Logistic/MLP/transformer and policy variants; propensity-matched nearest-neighbor cohort is a clinical comparator
state_fidelity_metrics: Transition accuracy/AUC; outcome AUC/F1; individualized risk displays and physician case-study judgments
transition_metrics: Stage-specific transition prediction and survival/toxicity performance at several outcome horizons
rollout_stability: NI: no quantitative free-rollout drift, divergence or joint-state constraint analysis reported
action_sensitivity: Alternative treatment sequences and treated/untreated propensity-matched comparisons are displayed; at least five matches within a caliper are required, but no action-shuffle experiment is reported.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Monte Carlo dropout generates uncertainty intervals; interval coverage or calibration was not evaluated
external_validation: No external institution, geography or temporal cohort
decision_utility: Participatory design included three oncologists, formative work with 11 physicians, and two clinician-centered qualitative case studies; no prospective clinical decision trial was performed.
safety_evaluation: Visual uncertainty, multiple model views and design for healthy skepticism are discussed; no explicit harmful-recommendation or recovery test
statistical_analysis: Descriptive model metrics and qualitative case-study analysis; NI: comprehensive inferential testing was not reported
causal_language: The title and system use intervention/counterfactual language; propensity matching supports comparison but does not identify individual treatment effects
estimand: Individual predicted trajectory under alternative treatment sequences; no explicit population estimand
confounding_strategy: Propensity-matched neighbor comparison only; residual confounding is not addressed
positivity_and_overlap: NI: propensity overlap and support diagnostics not reported
counterfactual_validation: No randomized, quasi-experimental, negative-control or target-trial validation
code_access: No public source-code repository was located from the paper, DOI, arXiv source or targeted repository search
weights_access: Unavailable/unclear: no released study weights located
data_access: Patient-level oncology data are not public
preprocessing_reproducibility: Architecture and features are described, but end-to-end preprocessing and data path are not publicly reproducible
randomness: Monte Carlo dropout is repeated; training seeds and repeated model fits are NI
evidence_anchors: Accepted author manuscript arXiv:2407.13107, Sections 3-5, Figs. 5-8, quantitative tables, and Appendix A.2. Main text reports n=526, while Appendix A.2 reports n=536=389+147; both values are retained as an unresolved publication inconsistency.
appraisal_strengths: Sequential treatment representation, multi-horizon outcomes, uncertainty display and direct clinician-centered evaluation
appraisal_limitations: Single-center retrospective data; unresolved 526-versus-536 cohort-count inconsistency; incomplete censoring/confounding and overlap characterization; no external/prospective validation, formal calibration, public pipeline, or hazard test.
source_status: Primary accepted author manuscript inspected; peer-reviewed IEEE TVCG DOI verified.

title: Digital twin brain simulator for real-time consciousness monitoring and virtual intervention using primate electrocorticogram data
domain: Primate neurophysiology; consciousness/anesthesia; ECoG digital twin
dataset_or_cohort: Neurotycho macaque ECoG recordings in awake and ketamine-medetomidine anesthesia conditions
sample_scale: Four macaques; 20 selected electrodes from 10 regions; 72 two-second sequences (144,000 modeled time steps reported) from three animals for core training, with the fourth used as held-out subject in four-fold analyses.
institution_count: NI: Neurotycho collection source is named, but recording-site count is not explicitly stated
split_strategy: Four-fold leave-one-animal-out: three macaques train and one tests; repeated across animals
observation_process: 1 kHz ECoG from 128 electrodes, reduced to 20 channels; awake/anesthetized sequences and online assimilation windows
missingness: Outlier time bins exceeding 8 SD and neighbors removed; 1.4% anesthetized and 8.6% awake data removed; no missingness model
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: fixed neurophysiology sequences; no time-to-event endpoint
state: Hierarchical stochastic latent variables representing local, network and global brain states
observation_decoder: Twenty-channel ECoG trajectories and latent state/condition classifications
action: Set global, network or regional latent states to emulate anesthesia/awakening or focal intervention
action_provenance: Purely virtual latent manipulation; analogized to drug, TMS or tDCS intervention
transition_mechanism: Hierarchical variational recurrent neural network with online error-regression/data assimilation
maximum_horizon: Supplementary prediction errors are reported from 1 to 100 free-running steps; virtual intervention is simulated for 2,000 steps, while online assimilation uses rolling 500-observation windows with 100 update steps.
rollout_regime: Stochastic free generation with online observation assimilation; offline virtual intervention
capability_claim: Action-conditioned simulation: generate ECoG after global, network-level or regional latent intervention
baselines: Observed ECoG and condition classifiers; no strong independent dynamical baseline reported for interventions
state_fidelity_metrics: Power spectra, functional connectivity, prediction error, latent clustering and condition-discriminator accuracy
transition_metrics: Held-out transition-sequence prediction and classification before/after assimilation or intervention
rollout_stability: Prediction error is reported across 1-100 free-running steps and online assimilation is repeated; no explicit physiological constraint-violation or very-long-horizon stability audit is reported.
action_sensitivity: Global z3, network z2 and regional z1 interventions; several intervention targets are compared
calibration_and_uncertainty: Variational stochastic samples/posteriors are used, but no reliability, ECE or coverage calibration
external_validation: Leave-one-animal-out testing is followed by assimilation/adaptation on the held-out animal; this is adapted population transfer, not wholly frozen external validation.
decision_utility: No clinical decision outcome; virtual intervention localizes networks and tests mechanistic hypotheses
safety_evaluation: No physiological hazard, dose limit, failure recovery or real intervention safety evaluation
statistical_analysis: Two-way ANOVA, t-tests, silhouette analyses and reported P values
causal_language: Virtual intervention and digital-twin language is used without an identified causal treatment effect
estimand: NA: simulated latent-state response rather than a population intervention estimand
positivity_and_overlap: NA: no real treatment support/overlap analysis
counterfactual_validation: Condition classification and known-state transitions validate simulations indirectly; no real intervention counterfactual
code_access: Core PV-RNN implementation public at https://github.com/h-idei/pvrnn_sa; Apache-2.0 license
weights_access: Unclear: repository includes example trained arrays, but study-specific macaque simulator weights were not clearly identified
data_access: Neurotycho data are publicly accessible under its terms
preprocessing_reproducibility: Electrode selection, normalization, sequence construction, model, assimilation, and intervention settings are described; public Neurotycho data and a generic PV-RNN implementation exist, but study-specific training configuration and weights were not confirmed.
randomness: Stochastic sequence sets and cross-animal folds are reported; fixed training seeds are NI
evidence_anchors: npj Digital Medicine PMCID PMC11811282: Methods on ECoG data, hierarchical V-RNN, data assimilation, and virtual intervention; Figs. 2-5, Table 1, supplementary 1-100-step prediction results, and 2,000-step intervention; Data Availability; h-idei/pvrnn_sa repository checked.
appraisal_strengths: Leave-one-animal evaluation, explicit hierarchical states, horizon-resolved free simulation, online assimilation, and multi-level virtual intervention sensitivity.
appraisal_limitations: Only four animals; held-out-subject evidence becomes adapted after assimilation; intervention remains latent/model-based; no formal calibration, real intervention validation, hazard test, or confirmed study-specific weights/configuration.
source_status: Primary peer-reviewed full text and supplementary results inspected; public data statement and generic implementation checked.

title: Koopman-based linearization of preparatory EEG dynamics in Parkinson's disease during galvanic vestibular stimulation.
publication_status: Peer-reviewed Frontiers in Human Neuroscience article; 2025
domain: EEG; Parkinson disease; neuromodulation and control
dataset_or_cohort: University of British Columbia Parkinson and healthy-control EEG/GVS study
sample_scale: 18 Parkinson participants and 18 selected healthy controls; seven medication/stimulation condition groups; 10 trials per block
split_strategy: Six-fold subject-level cross-validation with 15 training and 3 test subjects in each condition-specific group
observation_process: Twenty-seven-channel 1 kHz EEG during a one-second movement-preparation interval; five regional signals used by the model
missingness: Two Parkinson records were excluded for noise and 18 of 22 healthy controls were selected; no missing-data model
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: fixed EEG trials; no time-to-event outcome
state: Five regional EEG features encoded into a three-dimensional Koopman latent state
observation_decoder: Reconstructed/predicted EEG state trajectories and latent trajectories
action: LQR latent control intended to move PD-Off dynamics toward healthy-control reference
action_provenance: Simulated identity-matrix latent control; actual GVS/levodopa are observed experimental conditions but not the modeled LQR dose
transition_mechanism: Deep autoencoder with linear Koopman latent transition and linear-quadratic regulator
maximum_horizon: Recursive prediction error is reported from 1 through 15 steps (with 10-step error highlighted); the LQR tracking horizon is shown but not separately specified as a clinical time horizon.
rollout_regime: Free-running latent prediction across 1-15 steps and simulated closed-loop LQR trajectory tracking.
capability_claim: Planning: compute a control sequence to drive PD latent dynamics toward a healthy reference
baselines: Healthy, PD-Off/On, sham, GVS1, and GVS2 condition comparisons plus uncontrolled versus LQR-controlled trajectories; no strong independent sequence-model baseline.
state_fidelity_metrics: EEG reconstruction, latent trajectories/eigenvalues, spatial contribution maps, normalized mean-square error, and correlations with motor measures.
transition_metrics: Horizon-resolved normalized prediction error over 1-15 recursive steps; a 10-step error below 0.02 is highlighted.
rollout_stability: Horizon-specific error is reported over 1-15 steps and mapped LQR controls remain bounded in the example; no physiological constraint or long-horizon failure audit.
action_sensitivity: Controlled versus uncontrolled trajectories and different clinical/GVS condition dynamics are compared
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI: no predictive uncertainty or formal calibration reported
external_validation: No external institution, device or population validation
decision_utility: LQR demonstrates offline neuromodulation-control feasibility only
safety_evaluation: Bounded control is a limited constraint proxy; no physiological dose, adverse event or recovery analysis
statistical_analysis: Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality tests, ANOVA, Bonferroni correction and Pearson correlations
causal_language: The article states that GVS restores healthier EEG patterns and proposes targeted neuromodulation, but the LQR effect is model-based and no explicit treatment-effect estimand is identified.
estimand: NA: latent trajectory-control target rather than an identified treatment effect
confounding_strategy: Experimental GVS/sham and medication conditions reduce some confounding for observed contrasts; the proposed LQR intervention remains a model simulation.
positivity_and_overlap: No formal positivity/overlap analysis; observed stimulation conditions are defined, while simulated identity-matrix controls extend in latent space.
counterfactual_validation: No empirical validation of LQR-proposed intervention; condition differences provide indirect domain checks
weights_access: Unclear: no complete set of trained study weights identified
data_access: Full EEG request-based; repository supplies sample preprocessed HC train/validation/test data
preprocessing_reproducibility: EEG preprocessing, model, cross-validation and postprocessing are described; public sample data are incomplete
randomness: Cross-validation is reported; model seeds and repeated initializations are NI
evidence_anchors: Frontiers full text PMCID PMC12116581: participants and EEG preprocessing, six-fold subject split, Deep Koopman model, 1-15-step prediction (Fig. 4), LQR methods and controlled/uncontrolled trajectory with bounded inputs (Fig. 8), statistics, and Data/Code Availability.
appraisal_strengths: Subject-level folds, horizon-resolved recursive error, observed stimulation contrasts, motor correlations, interpretable linear control, and public code.
appraisal_limitations: Small single-site cohort and millisecond horizon; group-specific models; abstract identity-matrix control has no physiological dose mapping, explicit causal estimand, external validation, real model-directed intervention, or safety audit.
source_status: Primary peer-reviewed full text inspected through PMC; code availability checked.

title: Modelling neural coding in the auditory midbrain with high resolution and accuracy.
dataset_or_cohort: Large-scale inferior-colliculus recordings from anesthetized gerbils plus held-out animals and sounds
sample_scale: Fourteen gerbils total: nine development animals with 4,446 evaluated units, three additional animals for transfer, and two additional animals for neurophysiology tests; approximately 512 channels per animal.
split_strategy: Ten percent of training sounds form validation; all evaluation sounds are unseen; new-animal tests fit animal-specific decoders while retaining the shared encoder
observation_process: 512-channel recordings; multi-unit counts in 1.3-ms bins; more than 10 hours of diverse sounds per training animal
missingness: Units with response reliability below 0.2 are excluded from evaluation; non-stationarity is modeled with time input; no missing-data model
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: stimulus-response recordings with fixed segments
state: Shared sound encoder latent representation plus time-conditioned animal-specific decoder
observation_decoder: Categorical distribution over 0-4 MUA counts for every unit and time bin
action: Sound waveform, class, intensity, noise context and timing act as exogenous stimulus inputs
action_provenance: Experimentally presented acoustic stimuli for observed data; arbitrary new sounds can be simulated
transition_mechanism: Convolutional encoder-decoder maps waveform and time stamp directly to neural-response distributions; not autoregressive neural-state transition
maximum_horizon: Thirty-second unseen evaluation segments; direct response simulation rather than recursive horizon
rollout_regime: Stimulus-conditioned feed-forward simulation; no free-running state feedback
capability_claim: Action-conditioned simulation: predict task-relevant neural responses under defined acoustic stimuli
baselines: Poisson, time-invariant, single-branch, LNP and Mel-spectrogram ASR baselines
state_fidelity_metrics: RMSE, log likelihood, Fano factor, explainable variance/correlation and neurophysiological response curves
transition_metrics: Direct stimulus-response accuracy; NA: no recursive transition metric
rollout_stability: NA: no free-running rollout; non-stationarity across recording time is explicitly evaluated
action_sensitivity: Multiple unseen sound classes, intensities, noise levels and neurophysiological stimulus protocols test stimulus sensitivity
calibration_and_uncertainty: Categorical predictive distributions and bootstrap CIs are reported; no reliability or coverage calibration
external_validation: Unseen sounds are frozen; new animals require decoder fitting, so cross-animal evidence is adapted rather than frozen
decision_utility: Frozen ICNet features are evaluated as an ASR front end and against a Mel baseline
safety_evaluation: NA: no clinical/physical safety claim or hazard test
statistical_analysis: One thousand bootstrap samples provide 95% CIs; random validation sounds and randomized stimulus presentations are described
causal_language: No causal or counterfactual treatment language; this is stimulus-response prediction
counterfactual_validation: Neurophysiology phenomena are tested on two new animals; no causal counterfactual validation
code_access: Public code, example notebook and model at https://github.com/fotisdr/ICNet; non-commercial academic UCL license
weights_access: Public pretrained ICNet weights and configurations in the DNN folder
data_access: Evaluation sounds and recordings for seven animals are public; full recordings require an MTA
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed sounds, recording, binning, training, validation and evaluation protocols; runnable notebook supplied
randomness: One thousand bootstrap samples; random validation selection; fixed training seeds are NI
evidence_anchors: Nature Machine Intelligence PMCID PMC12460167: Methods on animals, sounds, architecture, held-out sounds, transfer, and statistics; Results Figs. 1-5 on likelihood/RMSE, Fano factor, explainable variance, speech, forward masking, and adaptation; Data/Code Availability and official ICNet repository with pretrained weights.
appraisal_strengths: Large neural dataset, unseen-sound evaluation, distributional response metrics, transfer experiments and public pretrained implementation
appraisal_limitations: Anesthetized animal model; new-animal adaptation is not frozen; no recursive state dynamics, formal calibration or safety/clinical utility
source_status: Primary peer-reviewed full text inspected through PMC; official code, configuration, example assets, and weights checked.

title: Optimized glycemic control of type 2 diabetes with reinforcement learning: a proof-of-concept trial.
domain: EHR; inpatient diabetes; model-based reinforcement learning
dataset_or_cohort: Multicenter EHR development at Zhongshan and Qingpu hospitals; external XuHui hospital cohort; prospective Zhongshan deployment and trial
sample_scale: 12,981 inpatients and 119,941 patient-days in retrospective development/validation; physician evaluations include 40 internal and 45 external cases; prospective deployment includes 20 patients; the single-arm feasibility trial includes 16 patients.
split_strategy: Patient-level development/internal testing plus held-out external hospital evaluation; prospective deployment and single-arm trial
observation_process: Seven standardized daily time points combining glucose, demographics, laboratories, medications, insulin and ClinicalBERT-derived text features
missingness: Models ingest standardized temporal features; missing-data robustness is tested by randomly discarding glucose values; exact imputation details are partial
censoring_or_competing_events: Hospitalization truncates trajectories; trial reports completion and adverse events; no formal competing-risk framework
state: Recurrent hidden diabetes state from longitudinal observations and prior treatments
observation_decoder: Next-day seven-point glucose, within-target-range status, reward and insulin dosage trajectory
action: Insulin type and dose recommended at each sequential step
action_provenance: Historical administered clinician treatment in EHR; AI recommendations reviewed and adopted/rejected by physicians in deployment/trial
transition_mechanism: Transformer-based recurrent patient dynamics model coupled to a jointly supervised model-based reinforcement-learning policy.
maximum_horizon: One-day patient-model horizon with seven intra-day periods; prospective recommendations can be repeated for up to five days.
rollout_regime: Recursive patient-model interaction for policy optimization, followed by physician-in-the-loop real deployment.
capability_claim: Planning: optimize sequential insulin regimen through model rollouts
baselines: CNN, LSTM, transformer, traditional dosing, supervised policies and physician groups
state_fidelity_metrics: PCC, MAE, within-target-range AUROC, reward-outcome correlation, weighted interval score, blinded expert assessment, and prospective glycemic outcomes.
transition_metrics: One-day K=7 state and treatment rollouts; dosage MAE and weighted-importance policy value
rollout_stability: Observation-frequency stress test is reported; no multi-day drift or model-exploitation metric
action_sensitivity: Insulin types and AI-versus-administered dose differences are analyzed; no formal dose shuffle/removal perturbation
calibration_and_uncertainty: Bootstrap confidence intervals, predictive distributions, and weighted interval score are reported; no reliability diagram, ECE, calibration slope/intercept, or coverage-by-horizon analysis is reported.
external_validation: Frozen external-hospital retrospective evaluation, independent physician review, prospective deployment, and a registered single-arm patient trial; no external fine-tuning is reported.
decision_utility: Offline WIS, blinded physician comparisons, prospective workflow deployment and a 16-patient proof-of-concept trial
safety_evaluation: Hypoglycemia, severe hypoglycemia, severe hyperglycemia/ketosis, physician override, and prospective monitoring are explicit; no severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia with ketosis occurred in the 16-patient trial.
statistical_analysis: Bootstrap n=1,000, confidence intervals, paired tests, Wilcoxon tests, generalized linear mixed model and prespecified trial power calculation
causal_language: The study uses optimized-control, off-policy, and proof-of-concept efficacy language; retrospective policy learning remains observational and the clinical trial is small and single-arm.
estimand: The trial pre-specifies within-patient change in mean daily capillary glucose; model development targets optimized glycemic reward/regimen rather than a randomized treatment contrast.
confounding_strategy: Weighted importance sampling and supervised-policy constraints are used for retrospective policy evaluation, but residual time-varying confounding remains; the prospective trial is a before/after single-arm design.
positivity_and_overlap: Effective sample size is used for WIS, but treatment positivity/overlap diagnostics are incomplete
counterfactual_validation: External retrospective comparison, expert review and single-arm prospective trial; no randomized counterfactual trial
code_access: Public code at https://github.com/rlditr23/RL-DITR; Apache-2.0 license
weights_access: Public trained model and sample package through Zenodo record 8198049
data_access: Minimum reproducibility dataset public on Zenodo; full de-identified EHR data are request-based with IRB/MTA review
preprocessing_reproducibility: Feature schema, model training and inference commands are public; full NLP/EHR pipeline depends on governed data
randomness: Bootstrap resampling and random case selection are reported; fixed model seeds are NI
evidence_anchors: Nature Medicine PMCID PMC10579102: Fig. 1 model/deployment design; Figs. 2-4 and Extended Data for K=7 internal/external evaluation; Methods on data, model-based RL, prospective deployment, trial, safety, and statistics; Data/Code Availability, RL-DITR repository, Zenodo record 8198049, and NCT05409391.
appraisal_strengths: Large multicenter longitudinal data, patient-model rollouts, frozen external-hospital testing, clinician comparison, real workflow use, explicit override/hazard monitoring, registered patient trial, and public code/model package.
appraisal_limitations: One-day model horizon; no formal calibration or randomized clinical comparator; retrospective policy value remains vulnerable to time-varying confounding; the feasibility trial is only 16 patients and single-arm.
source_status: Primary peer-reviewed full text inspected through PMC; public code, model/data package, and trial registration checked.

title: Simulating the outcome of amyloid treatments in Alzheimer's disease from imaging and clinical data.
domain: Alzheimer disease; multimodal imaging and disease-progression simulation
sample_scale: 442 individuals and 2,781 longitudinal observations; 71 stable normal, 33 normal converters, 131 MCI, 105 MCI converters and 102 AD; follow-up 0-16 years
institution_count: ADNI is multisite; exact contributing-site count not reported in the article
split_strategy: No held-out intervention split; disease-severity time shift is tested on an independent cohort in supplement; intervention model fitted on the 442-person ADNI cohort
observation_process: Irregular longitudinal MRI, AV45-PET, FDG-PET and seven neuropsychological measures
missingness: Model estimation requires at least one visit with all modalities; subsequent missing modalities are handled by matching available measures
censoring_or_competing_events: Follow-up ranges 0-16 years and diagnosis conversion uses last available follow-up; no explicit informative-dropout/censoring model
state: Four interpretable latent coordinates for amyloid, metabolism, atrophy and clinical cognition linked to regional observations
observation_decoder: Long-term regional biomarker and clinical-score trajectories and simulated trial endpoints
action: Amyloid progression reduction at 50% or 100% initiated at selected years before dementia conversion
action_provenance: Hypothetical irreversible model intervention; not observed treatment assignment
transition_mechanism: Bayesian latent ordinary differential equation system estimated with stochastic variational inference
maximum_horizon: Interventions from 20 to 1 years before conversion with outcomes at conversion; natural trajectories extrapolate across the disease history
rollout_regime: Free ODE integration under natural and modified dynamics
capability_claim: Counterfactual: compare placebo/natural progression with alternative amyloid-lowering timing and dose scenarios
baselines: State-of-the-art disease progression time-shift comparator; placebo natural-progression branch
state_fidelity_metrics: Clinical-group disease-severity ordering and biomarker trajectory agreement; independent-cohort time-shift validation noted
transition_metrics: No held-out transition-error metric for long-term trajectories; simulated score changes are compared with trial observations
rollout_stability: Trajectory means and standard deviations are shown; no drift/constraint-violation evaluation
action_sensitivity: Explicit placebo versus 50% and 100% lowering across multiple intervention years and sample sizes
calibration_and_uncertainty: Bayesian posterior/stochastic variational model and trajectory SDs are shown; no formal reliability or interval coverage calibration
external_validation: An independent cohort is used only for disease-severity/time-shift validation in supplementary analysis; it does not provide frozen validation of the simulated treatment response.
decision_utility: Simulated clinical endpoints and power curves inform trial timing, dose and sample-size design
safety_evaluation: No adverse-effect, toxicity, subgroup worst-case or treatment-hazard model
statistical_analysis: Two-sided Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney tests, two-sided Student t tests, P<0.01 and trajectory standard deviations
causal_language: Authors state the model may be interpreted causally if the data capture the disease history, then explicitly caution that unmodeled mechanisms may drive amyloid
estimand: Clinical-score contrast at conversion under specified amyloid-lowering dose and start time versus placebo
confounding_strategy: Mechanistic ODE constraints only; no measured-confounder adjustment for treatment effects because interventions are hypothetical
positivity_and_overlap: NA inside the simulator; real-world treatment support/overlap is not evaluated
counterfactual_validation: Compatibility with prior trials and independent disease-severity validation; no randomized validation of simulated individual outcomes
code_access: No public implementation was identified in the paper or targeted repository search
data_access: ADNI data are credentialed through adni.loni.usc.edu
preprocessing_reproducibility: MRI/PET processing, parcellation, z-score construction and variational model are described; code absence limits reproduction
randomness: Stochastic variational inference is used; seeds and repeated model fits are NI
evidence_anchors: Brain Communications PMCID PMC8168944: cohort and preprocessing, four-component latent ODE/Gaussian observation model, intervention simulation and statistics, Figs. 3-7 and Table 2, Discussion causal caveat, Data Availability; the linked supplementary PDF could not be retrieved during adjudication.
appraisal_strengths: Interpretable multimodal dynamics and strong timing/dose perturbation grid tied to trial endpoints and power
appraisal_limitations: Intervention effects are model-assumption driven; no formal causal identification, calibration, treatment-hazard model or public code; external validation does not validate intervention response
source_status: Primary peer-reviewed full text inspected through PMC; linked supplementary file remained inaccessible during adjudication.

title: Towards Causality-Aware Inferring: A Sequential Discriminative Approach for Medical Diagnosis.
publication_status: Peer-reviewed IEEE TPAMI article; arXiv:2003.06534v5 author version inspected
domain: Medical dialogue; sequential diagnosis; patient simulation and reinforcement learning
dataset_or_cohort: Public MuZhi and DingXiang pediatric medical-dialogue benchmarks
sample_scale: MuZhi: 586 train and 142 test records, 66 symptoms, 4 diseases; DingXiang: 423 train and 104 test records, 41 symptoms, 5 diseases
institution_count: NI: benchmark records come from separate sources, but clinical institution count is not reported
split_strategy: Published train/test splits; five-fold cross-validation for simulator inferential ability; five random-seed runs; cross-dataset transfer after semantic symptom remapping
observation_process: Sequential inquiries over explicit/implicit symptom slots with yes, no or not-sure responses and final disease label
missingness: Unrecorded symptoms are the central missingness problem; propensity latent matching imputes responses from similar same-disease records
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: bounded dialogue episodes; no clinical time-to-event censoring
state: Current symptom-answer vector, visitation mask, disease probabilities and simulated complete patient states
observation_decoder: Patient-simulator answer to each inquiry and final disease diagnosis
action: Choose an unobserved symptom to inquire about or stop and inform a disease
action_provenance: Simulated inquiry actions in closed-loop benchmark episodes; passive human dialogue records supply factual symptoms
transition_mechanism: Propensity-based patient-simulator state update plus generative intervener, bootstrapped diagnosers and Dueling-DQN inquiry policy
maximum_horizon: Maximum dialogue length is one-third of symptom count: 22 inquiries for MuZhi and approximately 13 for DingXiang
rollout_regime: Closed-loop simulated interaction; simulator and policy consume updated generated dialogue state
capability_claim: Planning: choose sequential inquiries until an uncertainty-based decision threshold permits diagnosis
baselines: Original default-answer simulator, generative world model, PSM variant, DQN, KR-DQN and PG-MI-GAN
state_fidelity_metrics: Inferential Ability, Symptom Density, physician-rated naturalness and symptom-disease consistency
transition_metrics: Closed-loop diagnosis success rate in in-distribution, out-of-distribution and cross-dataset settings
rollout_stability: Decision threshold and maximum-step behavior are tested; no state-drift or constraint-violation metric
action_sensitivity: Counterfactual inquiry relabeling, matching variants, no-intervention/no-bootstrap/no-threshold ablations and threshold scales
calibration_and_uncertainty: Monte Carlo final-state samples and ten bootstrapped diagnosers produce means/SDs and a 6-sigma stopping rule; no calibration/coverage test
external_validation: Cross-dataset MZ-to-DX and DX-to-MZ transfer uses BERT-based semantic remapping, so it is adapted rather than frozen external validation
decision_utility: Closed-loop benchmark diagnosis against RL baselines plus six-physician patient-simulator evaluation
safety_evaluation: Decision threshold, forced maximum stop and possible human intervention are discussed; no explicit misdiagnosis severity or clinical recovery test
statistical_analysis: Five random-seed runs with means/SDs; five-fold IA; six-physician blinded evaluation with one-tailed significance tests
causal_language: Explicit counterfactual inquiries, potential outcomes, propensity matching, causal diagrams and do-intervention language
estimand: Individual potential symptom response under a specified inquiry is defined; no population clinical-treatment effect
confounding_strategy: Matching conditions on learned latent propensity and same disease; ignorability, consistency and SUTVA are discussed but not empirically established
positivity_and_overlap: Lack of overlap is discussed; no quantitative overlap diagnostic for benchmark inquiries
counterfactual_validation: Relabeled known symptoms provide synthetic counterfactual-answer checks; no real prospective counterfactual validation
weights_access: Unclear: no released pretrained model weights identified
data_access: MuZhi and DingXiang are public cited benchmarks; repository mainly supplies code
preprocessing_reproducibility: Network architectures, training episodes, hyperparameters, data format and evaluation protocols are reported
randomness: All main evaluation results average five runs with different random seeds; exact seed values are NI
evidence_anchors: Official author manuscript arXiv:2003.06534v5: framework and experiments pp. 1-10, Tables 1-7 and Figs. 7-10, Appendix pp. 11-19 on potential outcomes, overlap, datasets, training, human evaluation, and limitations; official CAMAD repository checked.
appraisal_strengths: Direct simulator counterfactual-answer metric, closed-loop baselines, OOD/cross-dataset tests, human evaluation and uncertainty-based stopping
appraisal_limitations: Causal terminology exceeds identification of real clinical outcomes; small pediatric benchmarks, adapted transfer and no calibrated uncertainty or clinical safety study
source_status: Primary author manuscript corresponding to the peer-reviewed TPAMI article inspected; journal DOI and official repository verified.
